title: I Let the Felt-Wetting Table Clock Catch the Mentor Who Camped My Batt

parts.text: I rolled batt two onto the table at 9:08 a.m. and mentor Helix was already wetting my numbered wool. The card said: ONE TABLE. NINETY MINUTES. BATT STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-seven, fiber member, holding a soap card that listed our merino. Helix shrugged. "Mentors are the wet." I photographed the card, the booking, and her bubble wrap on my batt. Then I asked for the table log. At 9:16 the studio pinged why Helix's name was on my wool. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Helix's bubble wrap on my batt during our booking.

social.video_title: She wet my numbered wool on my table — Part 1/2
social.description: Felt table, a mentor on my batt, a ninety-minute card she posted. I logged the wrap. Would you have asked for the table log?

parts.text: Helix called it a sample until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the wrap still. The batt went back to my roll. Helix ran her own ninety and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about full. Full is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Table policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE WET. I keep our merino on a labeled bin. Helix brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the wet — Part 2/2
social.description: Table log, numbered batt, and a second line on the card. Was a sample ever my wrap?
